title: Quarterly Sprint Lattice: Hosted API + Model Catalog Tactical Map
creator: Priya Nanduri
description:
Goal: produce a compact, execution-ready quarterly plan that ties Hosted API endpoint priorities to the model catalog rotation and OKR outcomes.

Scope: define priority endpoint lanes (Experimental, Standard, Cost-Optimized), assign model families for each lane, schedule canary windows and rollback triggers, and map required engineering and infra work (autoscaling, KV cache tuning, quantization testing). Deliverables are a one-page tactical map, a sequence of sprint tickets for eng/design/ops, and an OKR tie-back that describes how the work contributes to Q2 objectives (latency SLOs, unit cost reduction, and model health).

Constraints & assumptions: available Dedicated capacity for two conserved GPU pools through April; model onboarding throughput limited by evaluation runner capacity (~3 models/week); must preserve parity of streaming and tool-calling behavior when rotating models.

Success metrics: 5% median p50 token latency improvement on standard endpoints, 12% unit cost reduction on cost-optimized lane, zero high-severity regressions in canaries (monitoring via quality regression alerts), and a documented rollout sequence for 8 model swaps with canary + auto-fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: One-page tactical map reviewed and signed off by Eng, Console PM, and Solutions (PDF + Confluence page)
Sprint tickets created and estimated for all engineering and design tasks required to ship the first two model swaps
Canary schedule with test prompts and rollback triggers published to the rollout calendar
OKR mapping table that links each initiative to a measurable success metric and owner
Risk register with mitigation actions for capacity, regression, and compliance concerns
updates: 2026-03-02: Kickoff with Eng (serving/runtime), Solutions, and Console PMs. Agreed to three priority lanes and preliminary model families for each.
2026-03-04: Draft tactical map uploaded to Confluence (https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PM/PM-388233+-+Tactical+Map). Requested latency baselines from runtime team.

2026-03-06: Runtime team provided baseline deck (Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/fake/runtime-baselines) — p50 for standard endpoints = 140ms, cost-optimized = 230ms. Noted KV cache hit rate variance by customer cohort.
2026-03-08: Design review — Console UX minor changes requested: add per-route canary toggle and a compact failure reason timeline. Created DES-4121 mock -> linked in sub_issues.

2026-03-09: Risk discussion: evaluation capacity is a bottleneck. Decided to prioritize two high-value swaps for April and queue four lower-risk swaps for May. Action: ENG-6019 to increase eval runner parallelism (estimate 3).

2026-03-10: Leadership sync. Approved the tactical map subject to two follow-ups: (1) quantify rollback latency impact, (2) produce monitoring runbook for quality regression alerts. Added release tag catalog-2026.04
notes: Trade-offs: faster rotation cadence increases the risk of undetected quality regressions — mitigate with stronger eval suites and staggered canaries.
Quantization profile testing must include a small held-out prompt set to catch hallucination regressions (ask Research for 200 prompt seed).
Consider bundling cost-optimized lane swaps with intelligent batching experiments to compound unit-cost gains.
